eligibility.quote: It only appears to be a problem with roscpp subscribers; rospy subscribers are unaffected, and setups which don't use ROS_IP or ROS_HOSTNAME on the publisher are also unaffected.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: a talker/listener reproducer and lost messages are documented. E2: separate processes exchange the advertised TCPROS endpoint; whether the publisher supplies an IP literal affects failure. This is a boundary-value-dependent parser defect, not deployment wiring or an internal failure with every correct peer. E3: PAIR.

failed_conditions.quote: It is definitely an issue in the modified code of `TransportTCP::connect()`.
failed_conditions.reason: other fits the consumer incorrectly parsing a valid endpoint host; there is no documented disagreement about the allowed encoding. requestTopic supplies the endpoint for the affected /chatter connection.

loudness.quote: With the roscpp nodes running in this setup, rosnode info /talker doesn't show any outgoing connections, but rosnode info /listener indicates that it's connected.
loudness.reason: The misleading connected state and missing messages document failure without a compatibility diagnostic.

detection_stage.quote: the rospy listener receives messages correctly; the roscpp listener does not
detection_stage.reason: The defect is noticed by missing runtime messages. Its mechanism is TCP connection establishment, but no connect-stage diagnostic is documented; retain run as the observed detection stage.

resolution.quote: Fixed, look for ros_comm v1.9.37 to come out.
resolution.reason: An accepted repair/upcoming release is documented, not successful reception by the identified pair at the fixed revisions; recommended is appropriate.

notes: The IPv4 sockaddr misuse and IPv6 branch correction belong to the same endpoint-parsing repair; no additional independently observed IPv6 composition is inferred. Non-literal ROS_HOSTNAME behavior is not established.

supporting_evidence.quote: Thanks for fixing it. I obviously misused the inet_pton function there.
